ball.a: Spreen, the streamer
ball.sub: He never touched the ball, and the game ended 1-1.

ball.q: In March 1999 Racing Club's members were told something extraordinary about their club. What?
ball.a: That it had officially ceased to exist, after going bankrupt
ball.sub: Fan pressure saved it from liquidation.

ball.q: Vélez Sarsfield went down in 1940, one point behind Atlanta. What had Atlanta done on the last day?
ball.a: Beaten Independiente 6-4, in a match suspected of being fixed
ball.sub: It is the only relegation in Vélez's history.

ball.q: Argentinos Juniors won the second division in 1940 but were not promoted. Why not?
ball.a: Their ground did not meet the requirements

ball.q: During River's 2011 first leg in Córdoba, hooded River fans ran on to the pitch. Who did they go for?
ball.a: Their own River players
ball.sub: The game was stopped for 20 minutes.

ball.q: Why did Temperley stop playing for two years from 1991?
ball.a: A judge declared the club bankrupt over debts to the players' union
ball.sub: The debt was about 400,000 dollars.

ball.q: Crucero del Norte from Misiones, who played in the top flight in 2015, are named after what?
ball.a: A long-distance bus company

ball.q: In October 2009 Martín Palermo scored against Vélez with a header from how far out?
ball.a: Almost 40 metres, about 38.9

ball.q: In 1999 Vélez's José Luis Chilavert scored a hat-trick against Ferro Carril Oeste. What was so unusual?
ball.a: He was the goalkeeper. All three were penalties
ball.sub: The first known hat-trick by a keeper in professional football.

ball.q: In 1980 Boca keeper Hugo Gatti said that gordito, little fatty, Maradona would not score past him. What happened when they met?
ball.a: Maradona scored four past him
ball.sub: Argentinos Juniors won 5-3.

ball.q: Carlos Tevez scored for Boca at River in the 2004 Libertadores and was sent off for his celebration. What did he do?
ball.a: Flapped his arms like a chicken
ball.sub: Gallinas, chickens, is the Boca fans' name for River.

ball.q: Riquelme scored against River in 2001, ran to the president's box and cupped his ears. Which puppet is it named after?
ball.a: Topo Gigio, the mouse
ball.sub: He said it was for his daughter, who loved Topo Gigio.

ball.q: In a 1974 friendly, Argentina's coach asked for one Rosario player to be taken off at half-time. Who was he?
ball.a: Tomás El Trinche Carlovich
ball.sub: Maradona later told him: you were better than me.

ball.q: What did Diego Maradona do with one of his first touches as a professional, against Talleres in 1976?
ball.a: Nutmegged Juan Domingo Cabrera

ball.q: A newspaper offered a prize to the first keeper to keep out River's Bernabé Ferreyra. Why was the winner a strange choice?
ball.a: He still conceded a goal, the game ended 1-1
ball.sub: Huracán's Cándido De Nicola took the prize anyway.

ball.q: Isidro Lángara scored four on his San Lorenzo debut against River in 1939. What made it even more remarkable?
ball.a: He had only arrived in Argentina that morning

ball.q: Maradona's last professional match was Boca's 2-1 win at River in October 1997. Who replaced him at half time?
ball.a: Juan Román Riquelme

ball.q: Carlos Tevez was sent off after scoring against River in the 2004 Copa Libertadores. How had he celebrated?
ball.a: By flapping his arms like a chicken, the nickname Boca fans give River

ball.q: With all four River keepers out with Covid in May 2021, who went in goal and helped beat Santa Fe 2-1?
ball.a: Enzo Pérez, an injured midfielder

ball.q: Martín Palermo scored for Boca against Vélez in 2009 from almost 39 metres out. With which part of his body?
ball.a: His head
ball.sub: It was his 200th Primera goal and won the game 3-2.

ball.q: Martín Palermo came back from six months out with a torn knee ligament in May 2000. What did he do in his first 15 minutes?
ball.a: Scored against River in a Copa Libertadores quarter-final

ball.q: Before a 1980 match Boca keeper Hugo Gatti called Maradona a bit chubby. What did Maradona do to him?
ball.a: Scored four past him in a 5-3 win for Argentinos Juniors

ball.q: Independiente's teenage star Sergio Agüero later married the daughter of which man?
ball.a: Diego Maradona
ball.sub: He married Giannina Maradona, and their son Benjamín was born in 2009.

ball.q: River beat Alianza Lima 8-1 in the 2022 Copa Libertadores. How many of the goals did Julián Álvarez score?
ball.a: Six

ball.q: In March 1999 the official running a bankrupt Racing Club made a famous announcement. What was it?
ball.a: That Racing Club had ceased to exist
ball.sub: She later said she did it to wake the fans up. They were champions in 2001.

ball.q: In 1996 Estudiantes keeper Carlos Bossio did something against Racing no Argentine keeper had done. What?
ball.a: Scored with a header, from a corner
ball.sub: It earned Estudiantes a draw.

ball.q: When Maradona brought his Gimnasia side to Newell's in 2019, what had the home club put beside the away bench for him?
ball.a: A throne
ball.sub: Gimnasia then won 4-0.

ball.q: Maradona promised Claudio Caniggia something for every goal against River. Caniggia scored three in 1996. What was it?
ball.a: A kiss
ball.sub: Boca won 4-1 at the Bombonera.

ball.q: Every 19 December, Rosario Central fans gather so Aldo Poy can do what?
ball.a: Re-enact his 1971 diving header against Newell's
ball.sub: He scores it again every time.

ball.q: Deportivo Riestra started a top-flight game against Vélez in 2024 with Spreen in the side. Who is Spreen?
ball.a: A streamer and influencer. He came off after about a minute

ball.q: Rosario Central refused to play a 1920s charity match for a leprosy clinic. What nickname did Newell's earn by playing it?
ball.a: Los Leprosos, the lepers
ball.sub: Central became Los Canallas, the scoundrels.

ball.q: Every 19 December, Rosario Central fans re-enact one goal, and the scorer himself scores it again. Which goal?
ball.a: Aldo Poy's diving header, the Palomita, against Newell's in 1971
ball.sub: In Cuba in 1997, Che Guevara's youngest son played Poy.

ball.q: Sent off in the 1967 play-off against Racing in Montevideo, how was Celtic's Bobby Lennox ushered off?
ball.a: By a policeman with a drawn sword
ball.sub: Bertie Auld was also sent off and simply stayed on.

ball.q: São Paulo won the 2012 Copa Sudamericana final against Tigre at half-time. Why?
ball.a: Tigre refused to come out for the second half, saying they had been attacked at half-time

ball.q: Boca offered to pay for surgery on the scar Carlos Tevez got from boiling water as a baby. What did he say?
ball.a: No. He kept it, saying it is part of who he is

ball.q: River Plate spent the world record fee from Omar Sívori's sale to Juventus in 1957 on what?
ball.a: Finishing El Monumental, with a fourth stand that bears his name

ball.q: River Plate are nicknamed Los Millonarios, the millionaires. Where does the name come from?
ball.a: Their big-money signings in the 1930s, above all a world record fee for Bernabé Ferreyra
ball.sub: They paid Tigre for him in 1932.

ball.q: In 1981 River Plate dropped their bid for Diego Maradona to keep which two stars?
ball.a: Daniel Passarella and Ubaldo Fillol
ball.sub: So Maradona went to Boca instead.

ball.q: Real Madrid pulled out of signing which Independiente defender in 2003 over his knee, only for Barcelona to buy him four years later?
ball.a: Gabriel Milito
ball.sub: He went to Real Zaragoza instead.

ball.q: Ariel Ortega never came back from international duty in 2003, and FIFA ordered him to pay 11 million dollars. To which Turkish club?
ball.a: Fenerbahçe
ball.sub: Newell's paid part of his debt to sign him in 2004.

ball.q: Daniele De Rossi joined Boca Juniors in 2019. How many games did he play before retiring that January?
ball.a: Seven
ball.sub: He announced it on 6 January 2020, for family reasons.

ball.q: Which Brazilian scored ten goals in seven Superclásicos for Boca Juniors in the early 1960s?
ball.a: Paulo Valentim
ball.sub: He came from Botafogo.

ball.q: Which two Boca Juniors players crossed straight over to River Plate in 1985?
ball.a: Oscar Ruggeri and Ricardo Gareca
ball.sub: Many Boca fans held it against Gareca for years.
